# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_011_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 11

**1** Jesus said: "This sky will pass away, and the one above it will pass away.

**2** The dead are not alive, and the living will not die.

**3** In the days when you consumed the dead, you made it living.

**4** When you come to dwell in the light, what will you do?

**5** On the day when you were one, you became two. But when you become two, what will you do?"

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**"This sky... the one above it"** — LOGOS preferred. The cosmological hierarchy (multiple heavens) is implied. Thomas does not elaborate.

**"Consumed the dead, you made it living"** — consensus. The transformative act of spiritual digestion: the practitioner who engages with the dead world enlivens it through the act of gnosis.

**"Come to dwell in the light"** — consensus. The transformed state is spatial ("dwell") and qualitative ("light").

**"Were one, became two"** — consensus. The movement from primal unity to duality is the existential problem Thomas addresses. The question "what will you do?" is the challenge posed to the reader.

**Synoptic Parallels:** No direct parallel. The cosmological language (passing heavens) has resonance with Matt 24:35 / Mark 13:31 ("heaven and earth will pass away") but the context is entirely different.

**Theological Note:** Saying 11 is programmatic for Thomas's anthropology: the problem is duality (having become two); the solution is reunification (becoming one again — cf. Sayings 4, 22, 106). The questions at the end of vv.4-5 are directed at the reader.
